# pangolin_custom_dns_record (Resource)

Manages a custom DNS record served by Pangolin's own nameservers, for a domain delegated to Pangolin (`pangolin_domain` with `type = "ns"`, not shared with another organization). Requires Pangolin 1.26.0 or later and an enterprise license.

Pangolin normalises records; the provider asks for that form instead of rewriting it, so what is written is what is stored: `name` relative to the domain and lowercase (`@` for the apex), hostnames lowercase without a trailing dot, TXT values without surrounding quotes. Pangolin keeps one record per name and type (and per priority / weight / port for MX and SRV): put several values in `values`. It refuses names it serves itself (resources, login pages, redirects, `_acme-challenge`) and caps a domain at 100 records and a name at 10 values per type.

Import with `{domain_id}/{id}`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A domain delegated to Pangolin's nameservers (Pangolin 1.26.0+, enterprise).
resource "pangolin_domain" "zone" {
  base_domain = "example.org"
  type        = "ns"
}

# Names are relative to the domain ("@" for the apex), lowercase, and
# hostnames have no trailing dot: the form Pangolin stores.
resource "pangolin_custom_dns_record" "mx" {
  domain_id = pangolin_domain.zone.id
  name      = "@"
  type      = "MX"
  values    = ["mail.example.net"]
  priority  = 10
}

resource "pangolin_custom_dns_record" "spf" {
  domain_id = pangolin_domain.zone.id
  name      = "@"
  type      = "TXT"
  values    = ["v=spf1 mx -all"] # no surrounding quotes
  ttl       = 3600
}

# Several values go into one record: one record per name and type.
resource "pangolin_custom_dns_record" "delegation" {
  domain_id = pangolin_domain.zone.id
  name      = "lab"
  type      = "NS"
  values    = ["ns1.example.net", "ns2.example.net"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (String) The ID of the domain (type `ns`). Changing it replaces the record.
- `name` (String) The name relative to the domain, lowercase: `@` for the apex, `www`, `_dmarc`, `*.apps` (a wildcard only as the leftmost label).
- `type` (String) The record type: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `NS`, `SRV` or `TXT`.
- `values` (List of String) The record data, one resource record per entry (1 to 10, no duplicates): an IPv4 address for `A`, a lowercase IPv6 address for `AAAA`, a lowercase hostname without a trailing dot for `CNAME` (one value), `MX`, `NS` and `SRV`, printable ASCII without surrounding quotes for `TXT` (up to 1024 characters).

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the record is served. Defaults to `true`.
- `port` (Number) Port, required for `SRV` and not allowed for other types.
- `priority` (Number) Priority, required for `MX` and `SRV` and not allowed for other types.
- `ttl` (Number) Time to live in seconds, 60 to 86400. Defaults to `300`.
- `weight` (Number) Weight, required for `SRV` and not allowed for other types.

### Read-Only

- `full_domain` (String) The fully qualified name the record is served for.
- `id` (Number) The record ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a custom DNS record as {domain_id}/{id}.
terraform import pangolin_custom_dns_record.mx <domain_id>/<record_id>
```
